guide.summary: A large top hunter that eats other hunters, but must keep hold of its prey before it can swallow it.
guide.biology: In real ponds, bigger predators hunt smaller hunters, so food chains can be several steps long.
guide.rules: Lives in water. Moves 1.2 cells per second and notices prey up to 6 cells away. Hunts Amoeba, Ciliate and Dartfin, which it must touch for 1 second without a break, and Shellglider, which takes 4 seconds. If contact breaks, the count starts over; prey wearing a mineral jacket take 1 to 4 seconds depending on how complete the jacket is. Stores a meal of up to twice its own body and waits 6 seconds after each catch. Uses 1.4 energy per second just to stay alive.
guide.example: Add one Needlejaw to a dish of Amoebas and Shellgliders and count which prey it catches more often.
